key_insight: Federated models showed high normal-versus-sick discrimination, but acquisition-year confounding challenges whether they learned genuine pathology signals.
clinical_relevance: These findings support further validation—not clinical use—before relying on federated breast-imaging AI to distinguish benign from malignant findings.
method: Compared CLIP, BiomedCLIP, and an ImageNet-pretrained ViT across two public breast-imaging datasets.
Evaluated federated training with and without client-level differential privacy.
Tested a text-free CLIP ablation and assessed patient-level performance, agreement, and communication cost.
evidence_signal: Normal-versus-sick ROC-AUC was 0.940–0.990 versus 0.974 for acquisition year alone; benign-versus-malignant ROC-AUC was 0.504–0.637, with all bootstrap 95% confidence intervals including 0.50.
watch_item: Differential privacy reduced ROC-AUC by 0.375, attributed to perturbing the full model state rather than only trainable parameters.
paper_title: Evaluating Federated Vision-Language and Vision-Only Models for Privacy-Aware Breast Cancer Imaging
